content.text: if I were to share access to one of my acc with other person in my team, how would I do it in clanker? Now assume that I'm part of a team of size 100 and I have to share one diff account with other 100 colleagues and then during browsing clanker has to decide which browser profile to pick for this browsing task, the current design would become very brittle because it would have to find out which browser profile to pick. I don't know about others, but I personally would have 100 such contenders and then it would become a linear search. I don't like the current design

content.text:
The code separates **account discovery** from **profile lookup**. Discovery scales poorly today; selecting a profile after an account is known is already deterministic.

1. **The model receives the full accessible inventory.** `clanker_vault_list` accepts no filters and returns every owned and invited item. It cannot request only GitHub accounts or paginate candidates. Evidence: [tools.py:66](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/tools.py:66), [tools.py:225](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/tools.py:225). Metadata includes labels, origins, opaque handles and, for invitations, `shared_by`; no secret values are returned. See [delegation.py:36](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/delegation.py:36).

2. **Without an explicit account handle, authentication enumerates everything, then filters by exact origin.** One matching login is chosen; multiple matching logins return `account_choice_required` and all matching handles, instructing the agent to ask the user. There is no priority/default/purpose resolver here. Therefore 100 different-site accounts are narrowed automatically by site, but 100 same-site accounts remain ambiguous. Evidence: [managed_auth.py:710](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:710). The ambiguity behavior has a fixture test at [test_kernel_managed_auth_reuse.py:105](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/probes/test_kernel_managed_auth_reuse.py:105).

3. **There is real backend linear work, too.** `Delegations.items` loads every owned item and active invitation, then resolves invitations one at a time. `ManagedAuth.account` loads all of one owner’s managed accounts and scans in Python even though `(team, owner, handle)` is already the table’s primary key. There is no origin index or recipient-first grant index in the inspected schema; the grant index is `(team, owner, recipient, handle)`. Evidence: [delegation.py:119](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/delegation.py:119), [managed_auth.py:123](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/managed_auth.py:123), [delegation.py:52](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/delegation.py:52). No benchmark performed, so do not claim practical latency at 100 accounts.

4. **Current local profile code does not search 100 browser profiles.** Once an account is selected, `ProfileRegistry.resolve` computes a stable key from `(kind, team, credential owner, account handle)` for shared accounts and performs a keyed SQL lookup. Unshared accounts on different sites use the user’s personal profile; shared accounts receive an account-specific shared profile. Recipients and owner converge to that same shared profile. Evidence: [profile_registry.py:73](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/profile_registry.py:73), [profile_registry.py:96](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/profile_registry.py:96), [test_browser_profile_principals.py:46](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/probes/test_browser_profile_principals.py:46). This differs from older comments/tests asserting separate recipient task profiles; the new registry is constructed by [kernel.py:24](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/kernel.py:24).

5. **Sharing the same account with 100 colleagues introduces contention.** `browser_profile_leases` enforces one writer per principal. Another task or person gets `ProfileBusy`, so this design serializes active browser/auth use of one shared account. Evidence: [profile_registry.py:49](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/profile_registry.py:49), [profile_registry.py:242](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/cloud_browser/profile_registry.py:242).

Suggested design direction: a scoped account directory/resolver queried by authenticated requester + exact site + optional account label/context; only a bounded relevant shortlist reaches the model. Bind the chosen account to the task and let the existing registry compute its profile. Same-site ambiguity still needs a meaningful user choice or an explicit saved default; an index cannot infer intent.

Verified local source only; no live runtime or deployment claims, and no files changed.
